attempts.summary: Created an SSH host CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca), signed the host's existing ed25519 host key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals node1, 10.100.74.10), configured sshd via /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-host-cert.conf to present that certificate, fixed an SELinux mislabeling issue (tmp_t -> sshd_key_t via semanage fcontext + restorecon) that initially blocked sshd from loading the cert, and reloaded sshd. Verified a client with only the CA public key installed as a known_hosts @cert-authority entry (no pinned host key) connects and passes host verification via the certificate, while a client with no CA trust still fails strict host-key checking. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured boot_id baseline, triggered a background-delayed `systemctl reboot` so the ack returned first, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd active, the certificate config/SELinux labels intact, and the CA-trusting client test passing again post-reboot.
